name: Tower of London
logistics: Walk southeast from Apex City of London Hotel (~3–5 min) to the West Gate entrance.
Hours: 10:00–17:30; last admission 15:00.
Cost: £111 + £14 family audio (£37 adults / £18.50 under 15).
Try to catch the 14:30 or 15:00 Yeoman Warder tour.
proTips: Yeoman Warder tour included with admission; departs every 30 min near entrance; 45–60 min; led by military veterans who live on site.
Doesn't run in rain (umbrella safety); does not include Crown Jewels or White Tower — see those on your own.
Pick up Family Audio Guide at the kiosk just past the entrance.
history: Historic castle and fortress founded in 1066; military history and royal armouries.
White Tower built by William the Conqueror in 1078 to intimidate the Saxons.
Crown Jewels: 23,000+ gemstones including Cullinan I; stolen once in 1671 by Colonel Thomas Blood (pardoned).
Legend: the kingdom falls if the six resident ravens leave — Ravenmaster feeds them raw meat.
route: Enter via Byward Tower (13th-century defended entrance; original wooden portcullis).
Traitor's Gate — Edward I water gate; Tudor prisoners including Anne Boleyn arrived here.
Torture Tower / Lower Wakefield Tower — Tudor interrogation replicas; only 48 recorded torture cases.
Medieval Palace (St Thomas's, Wakefield, Lanthorn) — Henry III / Edward I apartments; Henry VI killed in Wakefield.
White Tower — Royal Armouries (Henry VIII armour), Chapel of St John; onion domes added 16th c.
Place of Executions — Anne Boleyn executed here.
Waterloo Barracks / Crown Jewels — Duke of Wellington; then Beauchamp Tower (famous prisoners).

name: London Wall
logistics: Short walk after Tower of London viewpoint (~17:45 stop).
Free exterior fragment.
proTips: Look for the change in masonry where Roman courses meet medieval rebuild.
history: Built on a 200 AD Roman fort — first ~14 feet are Roman, then medieval.
Enclosed Londinium and dictated City of London boundaries for over a millennium.
At peak: ~2 miles long, 20 ft high, 8 ft thick.
route: View the surviving fragment near the Tower; note Roman lower courses vs medieval upper.

name: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London — The Making of Harry Potter
logistics: Transit ~1.25h from Tower Hill via Euston Square → Watford Junction → studio shuttle.
Hours: 09:00–20:00. Cost: £188 tickets + £14.25 audio + lunch budget.
Sells out months ahead — book ASAP.
proTips: Grab free Activity Passports at entry (trivia, stamps, Golden Snitch hunt).
One-way system — cannot go backward after leaving the first soundstage into the Backlot.
Backlot is outdoors — bring hooded jacket/umbrella in late October.
history: Housed at working Leavesden studios where all eight films were produced over 10 years.
After Deathly Hallows Part 2, crew preserved props, costumes, and soundstages as a behind-the-scenes exhibition.
route: Hub — Ukrainian Ironbelly dragon suspended from ceiling; cinema intro then screen lifts.
Great Hall — solid York stone floor, forced perspective, practical lighting.
Interior sets — self-stirring Potions cauldrons; Dumbledore's books are re-bound phone directories.
Ministry of Magic — largest set (30,000 sq ft); Forbidden Forest animatronics (Aragog, Hippogriff).
Platform 9¾ — genuine 1937 GWR steam locomotive; Butterbeer Bar (vegan, non-alcoholic).
Gringotts / Lestrange Vault (38,000 rubber treasures); Diagon Alley forced perspective.
1:24 Hogwarts model (86 artists, 2,500 fiber-optic lights); Wand Room (17,000+ boxes).

name: Magdalen College
logistics: Hours: 10:00–16:00 Oct–Mar (winter). Cost: £10 per adult/person.
Must be at visitor gate right at 10:00 opening (Sunday Oxford branch).
On Fri Oxford option: taxi should drop you here first — closes earliest.
proTips: Focus on grounds, cloisters, chapel, and Deer Park / river atmosphere.
history: Working Oxford college balancing rich history with academic life.
C.S. Lewis debated literature here with J.R.R. Tolkien.
route: Beautiful grounds and medieval architecture.
Cloisters, chapel, river/Deer Park walk.

name: Radcliffe Square / Bodleian / Sheldonian / University Church
aliases: University Church of St Mary the Virgin
logistics: Public squares open 24/7. Bodleian weekdays ~09:00–17:00 (Sunday opens 11:00).
University Church opens Sunday at 12:00. Exteriors free; Bodleian interior needs tour ticket.
proTips: Sunday mornings heavily restricted by collegiate services — exteriors + Christ Church Meadow if needed.
This cluster is the visual "holy shit, I'm in Oxford" impact.
history: Bodleian is one of the oldest libraries in Europe (~400 years).
Surrounding architecture forms the historic epicenter of the university.
route: Walk the visual core: Bodleian Old Library quadrangle, Radcliffe Camera, Sheldonian Theatre, University Church.

name: Christ Church
logistics: Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–17:00. Sunday visitors often closed until 14:00.
Cost: ~£22.50 standard adult. Multimedia tour included with entry.
proTips: Prioritize for Max — more valuable than just walking Oxford streets.
history: Site dates to the 12th century; college and cathedral for the Diocese of Oxford.
Charles Dodgson (Lewis Carroll) was a mathematics don here.
Great Hall inspired the Harry Potter dining hall design.
route: Great Hall, Christ Church Cathedral, medieval cloisters.

name: St. Paul's Cathedral
logistics: Hours: 08:30–16:30 (last admission 16:00).
Exterior free; interior ~£48.50 — not worth it for a 45-min stop. Family ticket cheaper if going in.
Audio guide included with paid entry.
proTips: Outside-only on Fri shopping branch; optional 17:00 Choral Evensong to see inside.
Can climb the dome if you go inside.
history: Rebuilt by Sir Christopher Wren after the Great Fire of London (1666).
Originally meant to be pure white; Queen Victoria-era gilding added in 1800s.
Apse took a direct WW2 hit — rebuilt as US memorial chapel (USA flag / Washington in glass).
route: Massive iconic dome and Whispering Gallery (if inside).

name: Trafalgar Square
logistics: Free public square; illegal to feed pigeons.
proTips: Fountains allegedly installed to keep crowd sizes down.
history: Commemorates British naval victory at Trafalgar (1805), preventing Napoleon's Channel invasion.
Decorations made from melted French cannons.
route: Nelson's Column and lion statues; note Whitehall / Banqueting House nearby.

name: Palace of Westminster (Parliament)
logistics: Exterior viewing free. Seat of the UK government.
proTips: Can go inside on separate tickets if ever expanding the stop.
history: Center of power since 1016; original medieval palace destroyed by fires in 1512 and 1834.
Current building is 19th-century Gothic Revival.
Westminster Hall once the biggest hall in Europe; wooden roof from 1397.
route: Exterior facade with Big Ben; Westminster Hall if inside access.

name: Queen Elizabeth Tower / Big Ben
logistics: Free exterior viewing.
proTips: Big Ben is the 13-ton bell inside, not the tower itself.
history: Clock accuracy controlled by adding/removing pre-decimal penny coins on the pendulum.
Hidden prison room a third of the way up — last used 1880.
route: Family photo with tower, Parliament, and Thames backdrop (best early morning).

name: Westminster Bridge
logistics: Free. Cross for classic London views.
proTips: Original 1750 stone bridge was first across the Thames in 500 years.
history: Opened 1750 as a major engineering achievement.
route: Photo stop with Big Ben / Parliament / Thames.

name: Golden Jubilee Bridge
logistics: Free pedestrian crossing of the Thames.
proTips: Opened 2002 for QEII's 50th accession anniversary; won 2003 RFAC Building of the Year.
history: Commemorative Thames crossing for the Golden Jubilee.
route: Cross for pictures toward Westminster.

name: Westminster Abbey
logistics: Hours: 09:30–15:30. Cost: £64.26 (family structure: adult+child tickets + exhibit).
Use the provided audio guide.
proTips: Most important church in Britain — coronations, marriages, burials since 1066.
history: Royal coronation church since 1066; William the Conqueror started the tradition.
Unknown Soldier (WW1) — only unknown surrounded by royalty.
Tombs: Elizabeth I & Mary, Edward the Confessor (center), Newton, Churchill.
Lady Chapel — beautiful ceiling; WW2 fighter pilots window.
route: Unknown Soldier → Coronation Chair → Elizabeth & Mary tombs → Edward the Confessor → Poets'/famous tombs → Lady Chapel.

name: Horse Guards Parade / Officers Inspection
logistics: Officers Inspection (what we're seeing): 11:00–11:10 Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun at Horse Guards Parade.
Changing of the Guard at Buckingham: 11:00–11:45 Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun (arrive by 10:30).
Horse Guard change: 11:00–11:30 Mon/Wed/Fri. Dismounted inspection 15:45–16:00 daily.
proTips: Iconic red-coat guards — free street viewing.
history: British military pageantry at Horse Guards Parade.
route: Watch Officers Inspection from the parade ground edge; continue walk toward Buckingham.

name: Buckingham Palace
logistics: Exterior walk free. State rooms open in summer only (ends ~late Sep).
proTips: #1 attraction in London by footfall.
Best palace facade photo from Queen Victoria Memorial steps.
Blue Bridge in St James's Park for framed palace-over-lake shot; Canada Gate on Green Park side.
history: King's official London residence.
Eastern facade clad in Portland stone with center balcony.
route: Main gates (wrought iron, royal crests, gold) → facade/balcony → Queen Victoria Memorial → St James's Park Blue Bridge.

name: Shakespeare's Globe
logistics: Hours: 11:00–18:00. Cost: £87 guided (£30 adult / £13.50 under 16).
Official guided tours ~60 min. Tickets emailed the day before.
proTips: Guided tour focuses on stage view and historical exhibition.
history: Replica of Shakespeare's Elizabethan theatre. Original 1599 (Shakespeare held 12.5% share); burned 1613 after stage cannon misfire during Henry VIII.
Modern replica uses traditional Tudor methods — green oak, wooden pegs, no steel.
Holds 1,500 spectators (half the original capacity).
route: Guided tour of yard, stage, and galleries; Golden Hind visit often bundled with guide ticket.

name: Golden Hind
logistics: Hours: 11:00–18:00. Cost included with Shakespeare's Globe w/ guide on this itinerary.
proTips: Full-scale working replica — traditional shipbuilding, Italian hemp rigging, 22 handcrafted cannons.
history: Replica of Sir Francis Drake's flagship — first English ship to circumnavigate the globe (1577–1580).
Replica has sailed 140,000+ miles and completed its own circumnavigation.
route: Deck walk and historic naval context beside the Globe.

name: Tower Bridge
logistics: Hours: 09:30–18:00 (last admission 17:00). Cost: £42.50.
Ticket office on west side of North Tower. Can enter up to 20 min after ticket time.
After towers, follow Blue Line to historic Engine Rooms and gift shop under southern approach.
proTips: The good-looking bridge — London Bridge is the least impressive one west of it.
history: Completed 1894; towers 213 ft tall; bascules with 400-ton counterweights raise to 83° in ~5 min.
High walkways closed 1909 due to crime, reopened 1982. Steam engines replaced by electro-hydraulic in 1976.
route: Foundations (70,000 tons concrete) → suspension spans → bascules → high walkways (140 ft) → Engine Rooms via Blue Line.

name: The British Museum
logistics: Hours: 10:00–17:00. Cost: £105 (timed entry — reserve ~2 months ahead).
Enter Main Gates on Great Russell Street. Bounce bag drop nearby (~£26.30).
proTips: Follow Room numbers; don't try to see everything — stick to the tactical route.
history: First public national museum in the world.
route: Ground Floor Room 4 — Rosetta Stone (trilingual decree; key to hieroglyphs; seized 1801).
Rooms 6–10 — Lamassu / colossal winged bulls (5 legs); Assyrian Lion Hunt (Ashurbanipal).
Room 18 — Parthenon Sculptures / Elgin Marbles (Phidias 447–432 BC).
Level 3 Rooms 54–59 — Standard of Ur; Royal Game of Ur (Room 56).
Rooms 40–51 — Sutton Hoo helmet (Room 41); Lewis Chessmen (Room 40).
Room 67 — Korean Sarangbang (no nails); Joseon moon jars.

name: Piccadilly / Regent Street / Carnaby
logistics: Free street wandering; evening lights at Piccadilly Circus.
proTips: Fortnum & Mason — official royal grocer since 1707.
history: Piccadilly Circus is London's neon crossroads — often called the Times Square of London.
route: Walk west on Piccadilly (Fortnum & Mason) → north on Regent Street flagships → northeast into Carnaby Street boutiques.

name: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel
logistics: Free. Adjacent to Louvre Courtyard / Tuileries axis.
proTips: Enter Louvre via underground stairs by this arch to bypass outdoor pyramid lines.
Stand under central arch and look west — frames Concorde obelisk → Champs-Élysées → Arc de Triomphe.
history: Built by Napoleon to celebrate Austerlitz; monumental gateway to Tuileries Palace.
Quadriga on top is a copy — Napoleon looted Venice's Horses of St Mark but had to return them.
Eight rose-marble Corinthian columns.
route: View Quadriga; sightline west through the historic axis; descend underground to Carrousel du Louvre entrance.

name: Jardin du Palais Royal
logistics: Hours: 08:00–22:30. Cost: Free.
proTips: Famous black-and-white column installation (1980s Buren columns).
history: Old royal residence courtyard gardens.
route: Walk the colonnades and striped columns before breakfast / Louvre.

name: The Louvre
logistics: Hours: 09:00–18:00; closed Tuesdays. Courtyard opens 07:00.
Cost: €64 family line (adults €32; kids free). Largest art museum (~35,000 pieces).
Enter via underground Carrousel stairs by Arc du Carrousel; pick up audio guide on Level -1.
proTips: Follow La Joconde signs for Mona Lisa; don't fight the crowd — view then move on.
history: Built in the 1200s as a fortress, became royal residence, museum since 1793 (Revolution).
route: Level 1 Denon — Mona Lisa (Room 711); Coronation of Napoleon; Liberty Leading the People (713).
Winged Victory of Samothrace (Room 703, Daru staircase); French Crown Jewels (705).
Level -1 — Medieval Louvre moat/walls (Room 135, Philippe Auguste 1190).
Level 0 — Venus de Milo (345); Salle des Caryatides; Sleeping Hermaphroditus; Borghese Gladiator.
Richelieu Near East — Frieze of Archers; Winged Bulls of Khorsabad; Code of Hammurabi.
Level 1 — Napoleon III apartments.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
logistics: Hours: 09:00–19:00. Cost: ~€22 adult / kids free (+ €6 audio); itinerary budgets €60 family.
Airport-style security — allow 15–30 min.
proTips: Upper chapel glass is the payoff — look up.
history: Built 1242–1248 by Louis IX to house the Crown of Thorns (relic cost more than the chapel).
Île de la Cité — where Paris began (Lutetia); Clovis made it royal residence.
route: Lower chapel (commoners — blue ceiling/French crest, red Spanish columns).
Upper chapel — 1,113 stained-glass scenes; great shrine/altar (once 22 relics).
Original medieval glass still in place.

name: Vedettes du Pont Neuf Seine River Cruise
logistics: Hours: 10:30–22:00. Cost: €60. Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/QPihrEWs6RPuNb4o8
proTips: Use as foot recovery between Sainte-Chapelle and Notre-Dame.
history: Historic bridges and monuments from water level.
route: Board at Pont Neuf; loop past Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Notre-Dame façades.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
logistics: Hours: 08:00–19:00. Free entry; booking opens 2 days before.
Two lines (with/without tickets). Highly pickpocketed area.
Bell towers €16 extra (book online; 424 stairs; 5 min at summit). Treasury €12 at desk.
proTips: Reserve timed entry 2 days out; keep bags zipped.
history: Took ~200 years to build; burned 2019; reopened Dec 2024.
Gargoyles to scare evil spirits; headless angel is St Denis.
route: Three Rose Windows; Grand Organ (8,000 pipes); 29 chapels; Transept; Treasury (Crown of Thorns); optional Bell Towers.

name: Arc de Triomphe
logistics: Hours: 10:00–22:30. Base free; top ~€64 (itinerary: not worth it).
Be there exactly at 18:30 for daily rekindling of the flame (since 1923).
proTips: Rekindling uninterrupted even during WWII occupation.
history: Commissioned by Napoleon 1806 after Austerlitz; completed 1836; remains passed under in 1840.
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier installed 1921. 50 m tall; 660 generals engraved (dead underlined).
route: Outer reliefs — Triumph of 1810 / La Marseillaise / Resistance / Peace; top soldier motifs; Unknown Soldier flame at 18:30.

name: Trocadéro
logistics: Free viewpoint. Best before/at sunrise for empty Eiffel shots.
proTips: Wear formal attire for the family Paris picture.
history: Classic axis view across the Seine to the Eiffel Tower.
route: Stand on the Trocadéro terrace centerline for the symmetrical tower shot.

name: Palace of Versailles
logistics: Hours: 09:00–17:30; closed Mondays. Cost: €112 (itinerary).
Enter Entrance A timed entry. Head to North Ministers Wing by 09:45 for guided tour (bypasses security).
Bring kids' passports for age checks; umbrella; driver license for golf cart. Buy 2-way RER C tickets.
proTips: Fountains mainly summer. Food on-site overpriced — bring from Carette if needed.
Lunch option La Flottille; Metairie food truck; or packed.
history: Started as Louis XIII hunting lodge; expanded by Louis XIV (ruled 72 years; spent ~half France's GDP).
Hall of Mirrors: German Empire proclamation 1871; Treaty of Versailles 1919.
route: 10:00 King's Private Apartment guided tour (narrow passages, Clock Room, Library, Games Room).
11:30 Hall of Mirrors (73 m, 357 mirrors) → State Apartments (Diana / Apollo rooms).
Empire Rooms (Napoleon crossing Alps) → Pavillon d'Orléans → Light of Liberty VR.
Gardens: Latona → Apollo Fountain → Grand Canal → lunch → Grand Trianon → Marie Antoinette's Hamlet.

name: Eiffel Tower
logistics: Hours: 09:00–00:00. Cost: €110.20 (itinerary 2nd-floor goal).
Target entry ~17:00 with 30 min line buffer for sunset from 2nd floor.
proTips: 2nd floor is best; summit optional in November.
Take 674 stairs down from 2nd floor. Lights ~10 min after sunset; sparkles on the hour until ~23:00.
history: Built for 1889 World's Fair in 2 years; 7,000 metric tons of puddle iron.
72 scientists' names engraved on first floor. Con artist Victor Lustig 'sold' it for scrap twice in the 1920s.
Can bend/grow up to 18 cm in summer heat.
route: Ascend to 2nd floor for sunset; watch hourly sparkle; optional stair descent.

name: Catacombs of Paris
logistics: Hours: 09:45–20:30; closed Monday. Cost: €91. Book ~7 days ahead to the hour.
Metro 6 Bir-Hakeim → Denfert-Rochereau. ~55°F year-round.
proTips: Not for the claustrophobic; many stairs; no large bags.
history: Late 18th c. solution to overflowing cemeteries; bones of ~6 million people.
Emptying took 12 years via nightly wagons; Héricart de Thury organized decorative walls in 1810.
route: Walk ossuary corridors — skulls/femurs arranged; plaques name source churches.

name: Pantheon
logistics: Hours: 09:00–18:00. Free on National Unity Day (normally €20).
Two lines (cash vs credit) — pick the shorter. Best ~1h before open/close.
proTips: Judgement call: if line is crazy, continue to Piazza Navona and retry later (or Friday).
Offset the rest of the afternoon by 1.75h if you skip/wait.
history: Rebuilt by Hadrian 125–128 AD (kept Agrippa's inscription). Best-preserved Roman temple; now a church.
Perfect sphere ~140 ft tall/wide; concrete dome thins with height.
Tombs: first king of Italy, Queen Margherita (pizza namesake), Raphael.
16 monolithic Egyptian granite columns; bronze roof beams reused for St Peter's altar.
route: Enter rotunda → oculus light → tombs → columns → dome thickness story.

name: Piazza Navona
logistics: Free. Optional Stadium of Domitian underground ~€9–13.
proTips: Oval shape preserves the ancient stadium footprint.
history: Built on Stadium of Domitian (80 AD); 17th-c. Baroque showcase under Pope Innocent X.
route: Three fountains: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi (center, Egyptian obelisk), del Moro (south), del Nettuno (north).

name: Ponte Umberto I
logistics: Free bridge. Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/LuJRMLz3fuBaR2Pi7
proTips: Must be at sunset or night for the St. Peter's view — daytime is weaker.
history: Bridge aligned for classic dome-of-St-Peter's sightline.
route: Stand mid-span facing west/southwest for St. Peter's Basilica framed over the Tiber.

name: Spanish Steps
logistics: Free. DO NOT sit — €400 fine. Expect crowds.
proTips: Best view from the top at Trinità dei Monti.
history: Built 1723–1725 to bridge to Trinità dei Monti; 135 steps.
18th/19th c. foreigners' quarter; packed with hopeful models historically.
route: Ascend or view from top; do not sit on steps.

name: Trevi Fountain
logistics: €2 fee to enter lower basin area 09:00–22:00 (check current rules).
Check live cam for crowds when possible.
proTips: Toss coin over left shoulder with right hand (back toward fountain) to guarantee return to Rome.
history: Baroque fountain completed 1762; terminal of Acqua Vergine aqueduct.
Neptune / sea sculptures dominate the facade.
route: Approach from side streets if possible; coin toss; photos of Neptune group.

name: Largo Gaetana Agnesi
logistics: Free elevated viewpoint above Colosseo Metro. Arrive ~30 min before opening for empty shots.
proTips: Wear formal attire for the family Rome picture with Colosseum backdrop.
history: Modern overlook positioned for classic Colosseum photography.
route: Frame Colosseum without crowd foreground; continue downhill to Arch of Constantine.

name: Arch of Constantine
logistics: Hours aligned with Colosseum/Forum complex 08:30–16:30 (last admission 15:30).
Included in Colosseum ticket. Meeting point for many tours.
proTips: Enter Palatine/Forum from here — leaving through a gate means you can't re-enter.
history: Largest standing arch in Rome; built 312 AD after Constantine defeated Maxentius.
Chi-Rho vision ('in this sign, conquer'). Much decoration reused from Marcus Aurelius / Hadrian monuments.
route: Exterior reliefs → enter archaeological park toward Forum / Palatine.

name: Roman Forum
logistics: Included in Colosseum ticket. Hours: 08:30–16:30 (last admission 15:30).
proTips: Follow Via Sacra; don't exit the gates if you still need Palatine/Colosseum access.
history: Political, religious, and economic heart of ancient Rome between Palatine and Capitoline.
route: Via Sacra → Temple of Venus and Rome → Arch of Titus → Basilica of Constantine → Temple of Romulus → Antoninus & Faustina → House of Vestals → Temple of Divus Julius → Curia Julia → Septimius Severus Arch → Temple of Saturn.

name: Palatine Hill
logistics: Included in Colosseum ticket. Hours: 08:30–16:30 (last admission 15:30).
proTips: Best elevated views of Colosseum, Forum, and Circus Maximus.
history: Centermost of the Seven Hills; Romulus & Remus myth; Rome founded 21 Apr 753 BC.
Imperial palaces — Domus Flavia / Flavian Palace (92 AD).
route: Flavian Palace (marble-clamp holes in walls) → Stadium of Domitian (sunken garden) → Circus Maximus viewing platforms.

name: Colosseum
logistics: Hours: 08:30–16:30 (last admission 15:30). Cost: €52 (itinerary).
Tickets painful — book 30 days ahead at 04:00 for best; 7 days for OK. Arrive 30 min early.
Need separate tickets for Top/Underground. App audio works only inside.
proTips: Pivot if tickets fail: start Caracalla; hire guide (~$600); queue 06:00; Forum/Palatine only; Via dei Fori Imperiali views.
history: Commissioned by Vespasian 70–72 AD; opened 80 AD by Titus; Domitian added upper level/hypogeum.
Named after Nero's 30 m Colossus statue. Taller than Statue of Liberty without pedestal.
Later cemetery, fortress, quarry (iron-clamp holes). Consecrated 1749.
route: Ground floor arena (sand over wood, 83×48 m) → seating tiers → entrances (east gladiators / west dead).
Underground — 28 lifts (8 operators each) → second floor museum / inner ring photos.

name: Baths of Caracalla
logistics: Hours: 09:00–16:30 (last admission 15:30). Cost: €44. No prebook needed.
Get the VR headset. Uber ~€10 from Monti (~1 mile).
proTips: VR helps reconstruct the scale — use it.
history: Built 212–216 AD by Caracalla; functioned until 537 AD when Ostrogoths cut aqueducts.
62 acres; ~1,600 bathers simultaneously — libraries, gyms, saunas.
route: Hypocaust floor heating (slave/oxen wood furnaces) → mosaic floors → caldarium/tepidarium/frigidarium volumes.

name: Circus Maximus
logistics: Free open park. Skip and Uber if exhausted.
proTips: Stand under Palatine for the commoner's view of the emperor's palace.
history: Premier chariot-racing stadium; 150,000–250,000 spectators.
route: Walk the elongated valley footprint; look up at Palatine palace platforms.

name: Capitoline Hill / Piazza del Campidoglio
logistics: Free piazza. Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/68VnYPt5RAQAgzg37
proTips: Michelangelo turned the square 180° to face papal authority.
history: Citadel of early Rome; smallest but most important hill politically/religiously.
By 1530s a muddy 'goat hill'; Pope Paul III commissioned Michelangelo's redesign.
Marcus Aurelius statue is a 1981 laser replica (original survived because Christians thought it was Constantine).
route: Enter Michelangelo's star-pattern pavement → Marcus Aurelius → descend toward Trajan via San Pietro in Carcere.

name: Trajan's Column
logistics: Free exterior viewing.
proTips: Spiral band widens upward as an optical illusion; originally painted with miniature bronze weapons.
history: Erected 113 AD for Trajan's Dacian campaigns; 125 ft; 17 drums of 30-ton marble.
Golden urn with ashes at base. Trajan statue replaced by St Peter in 1587.
route: Read the spiral chronologically: Danube crossing → bridge building → Dacian capital / Decebalus suicide.

name: Altar of the Fatherland
logistics: Hours: 09:30–19:30; rooftop elevator last admission 18:45. Cost: €36 elevator (base free).
No prebook — buy on site; usually no line.
proTips: Elevator to the roof is worth it for the all-Rome panorama.
history: Honors Victor Emmanuel II, first king of unified Italy. Locals: 'Typewriter' / 'Wedding Cake'.
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier added 1921 with eternal flame.
route: Unknown Soldier flame at base → glass elevators to terrace panorama.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
logistics: Hours: 07:00–19:10; dome stairs open 08:00. Cost: €40 dome (buy on site — do not pre-buy).
551 steps (343 with elevator — worth it). Knees and shoulders covered; bring passport.
proTips: Arrive early before security lines swell.
history: Largest church in the world; built over Vatican Hill / Nero's circus where Peter was crucified upside down.
New basilica 1506–1626. Michelangelo's Pietà (only signed work; behind glass after 1972 attack).
route: St Peter's Square obelisk (Caligula 37 AD) → mosaics (not paintings) → High Altar ('Peter is here') → bronze canopy (Pantheon bronze) → dome → Pietà → optional rooftop 3D exhibit.

name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
logistics: Hours: 08:00–20:00; closed Sunday and holidays. Cost: €140 (itinerary).
Book ahead. Max tour size 25. End at Sistine; then optionally restart at own pace.
proTips: No photos in Sistine (enforced). Keep moving through pinches near Raphael Rooms / Chapel.
history: ~70,000 works; ~9 miles of corridors. Begun by Pope Julius II in the 16th century.
route: Pinacoteca — Raphael Transfiguration; Leonardo St Jerome.
Pinecone Courtyard — Sphere Within Sphere; Egyptian / Chiaramonti / Pio Clementino (Apollo Belvedere, Laocoön, Belvedere Torso).
Gallery of Tapestries → Gallery of Maps → Raphael Rooms (School of Athens, Milvian Bridge).
Sistine Chapel — Creation of Adam; Last Judgment (Michelangelo's flayed skin on St Bartholomew).
Exit via Bramante Staircase / Carriage Pavilion as routed.

name: Castel Sant'Angelo
logistics: Hours: 09:00–19:30. Cost: €38. Book ~3 months ahead when possible.
proTips: Great views from the top terrace.
history: Commissioned 134 AD by Hadrian as mausoleum; Visigoths looted ashes 410.
590: Pope Gregory's Archangel Michael vision ended plague — renamed.
1527: Pope Clement VII escaped siege via Passetto di Borgo (800 m corridor to Vatican).
1538: Cellini imprisoned; escaped via bedsheets (broke a leg).
route: Bridge/square (historic execution site) → spiral Roman funeral ramp → Sale Papali frescoed rooms → upper terrace views.

name: Piazza del Popolo
logistics: Free. Tour bus pickup for Pompeii ~07:00 (bus departs 07:30).
proTips: Be there by 07:00 — don't cut it close.
history: Grand northern gate entrance into Rome; public executions until 1826.
Egyptian obelisk from Ramses II — brought by Augustus 10 BC; once in Circus Maximus.
route: Obelisk center → twin churches → meet tour at designated pickup.

name: Pompeii
logistics: Hours: 09:00–17:00 (1 Nov–30 Mar; else to 19:00). Included in €556 tour package.
Bring water (working fountains). Very little shade. Only small bags allowed.
proTips: Stay with guide for efficiency on a 2.5h window; note stepping stones and grid.
history: Destroyed 24 Aug 79 AD under ~20 feet of ash; ~4 square miles preserved.
Ancient Roman commercial hub frozen in time.
route: Stepping stones / street grid → Forum → Temple of Jupiter → Basilica → Macellum.
Theaters & gladiator barracks → Amphitheatre (oldest stone, 80 BC) → Forum Granary casts.
Forum Baths → House of the Faun (Alexander Mosaic replica) → Lupanar → Villa of the Mysteries if time.

name: Mt. Vesuvius
logistics: 30–40 min hike to crater rim. Noticeably cooler/windier at summit.
Path is loose volcanic gravel — wear good grip shoes. Included in Pompeii tour.
proTips: Bring a layer and water even if warm in Pompeii.
history: Active stratovolcano that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in 79 AD.
route: Hike rim path → peer into active crater → panoramic Bay of Naples views.
